corpus: mybodycorpai apps/web @ 51f9925 (99 files, 183 components after detector fix)

severityAnchors.P0: emitted suite broken, silently passes, or lies; or the tool corrupts user files
severityAnchors.P1: wrong analysis output, docs claim contradicted by code, or a CI gap that lets P0s ship
severityAnchors.P2: performance, DX, error-message quality, design friction
severityAnchors.P3: opportunity aligned with the product's spirit

findings.title: --run-tests / --changed suite failures never reached the exit code
findings.claim: runCore discarded both runners' outcomes; exitCode came from generation failures only, so --ci --run-tests exited 0 on red suites.
findings.fix: runGeneratedTests returns a boolean like runAffectedTests; both fold into exitCode. Guarded by tests/runTests.test.ts (a suite forced to exit 1 must yield false).

findings.title: bun src/cli.ts was a silent exit-0 no-op for every flag
findings.claim: cli.ts only exported main() and nothing called it — the same trap bin.ts's header documents for the compile entry. A real session lost an afternoon to it and blamed the sandbox (project memory 'flawless-cli-unreliable-in-sandbox').
findings.fix: import.meta.main guard appended; subprocess test asserts `bun src/cli.ts -V` prints the version.

findings.title: Ownership/regeneration claims contradicted the write-once model
findings.claim: README:21 promised 'no regeneration step that overwrites your edits' and extending.md:3/:99 claimed any re-run is refused without --force; reality is regenerate-by-default with a write-once protected set, and only the perf-harness scaffold refuses.
findings.fix: Both files now state the real contract (protected set named; refusal scoped to perf-harness; colocate as the guard for hand-hardened specs).

findings.title: Bad --nextjs input threw plain Error and exited 1 instead of 2
findings.claim: Docs promise 'bad input throws UsageError'; detect.ts's four throw sites used Error, so usage mistakes exited as internal errors.
findings.fix: UsageError moved to types.ts (no core cycle), all four sites throw it; test asserts instanceof.

findings.title: architecture.md profile-spec path and generated-suite.md click-rerender were pre-rework stale
findings.claim: architecture.md named tests/<Name>.profile.spec.ts (a path deliberately abandoned because `bun test tests` collects it); generated-suite.md described the first-button exploratory click the emitter explicitly bans.
findings.fix: Both sections rewritten to the current behaviour (profile/ path; derived click target with scaffold-time skips).

findings.title: Style adoption never formatted .mts, so the emitted vitest config broke the adopter's biome ci
findings.claim: FORMATTABLE had no mts/cts arm; vitest.config.mts survived in template indentation and failed `biome ci` in a tabs project while the log claimed every file was formatted.
findings.fix: Merged PR #1 (failing test first). Verified by dogfood iteration 1: post-fix regeneration is byte-identical with the committed tab-formatted config.

findings.title: Effect-only (return null) and base-ui useRender components were invisible to parseFile
findings.claim: Both dogfood 'no component could be read' files were ordinary modern shapes; the useRender pattern is what shadcn's base-ui port emits, so the miss recurs in every adopting app.
findings.fix: Merged PR #2: looksLikeComponentBody accepts all-own-returns-null and imported-render-hook calls (syntactic triggers only). Dogfood: 181 → 183 components, unreadable 2 → 0.

findings.title: Sweeps reported the project's own suppressions as unused-suppression findings
findings.claim: The scratch sweep config enables only the task's rules, so a biome-ignore answering a project-config rule was 'unused' there — answering the a11y task's one finding created a new react-rules finding.
findings.fix: suppressions/* diagnostics dropped in runBiome; test proves an out-of-set suppression yields no finding.

findings.title: Passing a directory (or the prompt's empty submit) produced two misleading messages
findings.claim: expandGlob treated any existing path as an entry file; a directory fell through to 'Directories cannot be read like files' + 'no analysable components found'.
findings.fix: Directory now throws UsageError naming the fix ('pass a .tsx file or a glob like …'); test added.

findings.title: The 'half a second' analysis claim was asserted in three places and pinned by nothing
findings.claim: No benchmark backed the number the --changed design leans on.
findings.fix: Measured 2026-08-23: 99 files → 463 ms median (matches the claim); extending.md now carries the dated measurement. A cheap timing assertion remains open as FR-024's suggestion.

findings.title: forwardRef<E, Props> and `const X: FC<Props> = memo(...)` silently lose the declared props type
findings.claim: The wrapper branch never consults the forwardRef call's typeArguments[1] nor the declaration's FC<Props>, so extraction returns an empty shape with empty unresolved records — a silent empty, confirmed by probe.
findings.proposed_fix: Capture wrapper type arguments in unwrapWrappers and prefer them as propsTypeNode; at minimum record an unresolvedTypes marker so the give-up is visible.

findings.title: A backtick or ${ in a clickable element's label breaks the emitted browser spec
findings.claim: describeClickLabel escapes only double quotes but is interpolated into template-literal titles; probe produced 'Unterminated string literal' in the emitted spec.
findings.fix: titleSafe (scaffold's escaper) now routes every scaffold-tests title interpolation; hostile-label fixture parses clean. (wave 1)

findings.title: Colocate vitest include hardcodes src/** — a src-less Next.js layout emits specs vitest never runs
findings.claim: Specs colocated under <root>/components or <root>/app match neither include glob; probe confirmed non-selection. (The finder's aside that mybodycorpai is src-less was wrong — it has src/ — but the shape is common elsewhere.)
findings.fix: Root-wide include globs + explicit standard excludes — run-order independent, covers src-less layouts; known --out-outside-tree limit documented. (wave 1)

findings.title: Dotted data-dep callees (db.query.users.findMany) are mocked as a function at the root binding
findings.claim: The emitted mock `db: vi.fn(...)` makes `.query` undefined, the RSC spec throws on correct code, and dep.uncertain is false so no skip fires — a hard false failure, confirmed by probe.
findings.proposed_fix: Emit a nested object with vi.fn at the leaf of dep.callee, merging deps that share a root; or mark dotted callees uncertain.

findings.title: mock/routes.ts promises 'no regeneration step will overwrite this file' but --force regenerates it
findings.claim: The file is pushed without writeOnce, so --force rewrites it from the OpenAPI spec, discarding hand-edited fixture bodies — against its own emitted header.
findings.fix: writeOnce: true on mock/routes.ts; survival test edits between force runs. (wave 1)

findings.title: host/main.tsx is write-once but holds the mount registry — a newly detected component's browser spec can never mount
findings.claim: Observed live: after the detector fix, Badge's fresh browser spec failed with 'unknown component: Badge' because no tool invocation (not even --force) can add it to the kept host. The registry is mechanical data trapped in a user-owned file.
findings.proposed_fix: Split the generated registry from the user-owned mount wrapper (registry file regenerated, wrapper write-once), or at minimum warn when emitted specs reference components the existing host does not register.

findings.title: --changed with the full task selection silently skips the affected-test run on an adopted suite
findings.claim: perf-harness's no-force refusal sets anyFailed, and the affected run is gated on !anyFailed — so the flag's primary use case (fast loop over an existing suite) runs nothing unless the user knows to narrow --tasks. Observed live in dogfood iteration 4.
findings.proposed_fix: In changed-mode, treat an existing harness as the normal case (skip scaffold instead of throwing), or run affected tests despite the refusal and say so.

findings.title: Emitted unit specs are listed, parsed and type-checked — but never once executed under real vitest
findings.claim: An assertion-body bug (wrong RTL API, jest-dom matcher, setup.ts runtime error) passes every repo check and fails in every adopter repo. The cached-suite infrastructure already pins everything an execution needs.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the cached suite: install the full emitted devDependency set, `vitest run`, assert >0 passed; guard the guard with one deliberately failing spec.

findings.title: runner/runTests.ts command planning is untested — the module two shipped bugs lived in
findings.claim: The script-planning branches (standalone vs Next.js, the browser gate, vitest related vs --grep) are guarded only by comments naming past regressions. (This review added outcome tests for runGeneratedTests; the planning matrix remains uncovered.)
findings.proposed_fix: Extract command planning into a pure function and assert the plan per task combination.

findings.title: The --json/--ci process contract is promised in the README and tested nowhere
findings.claim: No test spawns the CLI with --ci and JSON.parses the whole stdout; one stray log line before the blob would ship unnoticed.
findings.proposed_fix: Spawn against a fixture with --ci, JSON.parse entire stdout, assert {outDir, results} and exit codes (0 and 2 cases).

findings.title: The crust half of the baseline gate is a one-off manual run preserved as a comment
findings.claim: If crust renames summary.p95 the gate compares against undefined and passes vacuously forever; the Jenkinsfile installs jq/zsh/nodejs but not crust.
findings.proposed_fix: Install crust in CI from the apps plane and automate the documented manual run (no baseline / at-baseline / forced-fail cases), fail-don't-skip.

findings.title: No emitted playwright spec ever meets a real browser in this repo's CI
findings.claim: Hosts are booted and curled and configs --list'ed, but a spec-body runtime error against the __FLAWLESS__ driver API is invisible here.
findings.proposed_fix: One Jenkins-gated case: playwright install chromium, run the smallest browser spec against the booted host with real react, one green + one mutated-red.

findings.title: CI runs bun test and tsc but never the biome gate the repo declares
findings.claim: package.json declares check: biome check; no biome invocation exists in the Jenkinsfile.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `bunx biome ci .` to the Test stage.

findings.title: prompt.ts and the findings print functions are the remaining zero-execution modules
findings.claim: A FAIL rendered as ok, or a cancel that falls through to a run, would ship silently.
findings.proposed_fix: Capture stdout writes for the print fns; drive prompt.ts through its already-abstracted ClackPrompts interface with a scripted fake.

findings.title: `satisfies FC<Props>` components are not detected; as children they vanish silently
findings.claim: unitFromInitializer never unwraps SatisfiesExpression/AsExpression; as an entry the file throws, as a child the component is dropped with no record. Probe-confirmed.
findings.fix: unitFromInitializer peels satisfies/as/parens via unwrapTrivialExpression and harvests FC type args from the cast. (wave 1)

findings.title: provider.fixtures.ts doc comment breaks when dropped layout-prop source contains */
findings.claim: A layout prop like config={{ include: "**/*" }} terminates the /** comment early and the write-once fixtures file does not parse.
findings.fix: Comment-bound layout text sanitises */; fixtures file parses with globs in prop values. (wave 1)

findings.title: Utility modules like cn are auto-mocked — with an async stub for a sync function
findings.claim: Generated compound-part specs carry vi.mock("@/lib/utils", () => ({ cn: vi.fn(async () => ({})) })): the tool mocks the exact module its own docs say never to mock, and the stub returns a Promise where a string is expected (className becomes '[object Promise]' once the component renders).
findings.fix: Pure-utility exemption merged per specifier over imported names; mixed mocks carry sync join stubs under local names (aliases included). (wave 1)

findings.title: No minimal upgrade path: a no-force run over an adopted suite always exits 1
findings.claim: perf-harness hard-refuses without --force, so refreshing derived files costs exit 1 ('task threw' committed into REPORT.md), and --force is the only harness refresh — which also clobbers hand-hardened colocated specs.
findings.proposed_fix: A refresh mode between nothing and --force: regenerate derived files, keep the harness, exit 0 with an explicit 'harness kept (N runs old)' line.

findings.title: String-literal prop names ("data-variant") are dropped without a trace
findings.claim: walkMembers skips non-Identifier names before recording anything, violating the propPositions contract. Probe-confirmed.
findings.fix: String-literal prop names accepted end-to-end (DEFAULTS keys are JSON.stringify'd). (wave 1)

findings.title: hostEligibility's namespace-server-action exclusion is dead code
findings.claim: The guard requires names.length === 1 and then names.length === 0 on the same object — unreachable.
findings.fix: Dead namespace check replaced: importedNames landed on ModuleImportInfo, decision uses module-side names. (wave 1)

findings.title: --help/--version pay ~110ms importing the TypeScript compiler before argv parsing
findings.claim: Measured: core graph import 109ms median, 97% of it the typescript package; --help needs ~10ms.
findings.fix: core/tasks imports now dynamic inside main(); --help measured 131ms → 14ms, guarded by a latency test + structural no-top-level-value-import pin. (wave 1)

findings.title: Per-entry SourceFileCache/ModuleResolver re-parses shared leaves 1058 times per sweep (~13-19% of wall)
findings.claim: Measured: 1157 parseFile calls for 99 unique files; card.tsx parsed 237×. Costs ~100-160ms of a 825ms full run — real but small; the sequential loop itself measured NOT worth parallelising (~2.5% projected).
findings.fix: One shared SourceFileCache+ModuleResolver per sweep (analyse API additively extended); tag-root resolution threaded too; reference-equality + fetch-count tests. (wave 1)

findings.title: Value-taking flags disagree on missing values; --props errors hide the flag name
findings.claim: --depth/--variants silently default where siblings throw 'requires a value'; bad --props JSON surfaces a bare engine message.
findings.fix: --depth/--variants throw 'requires a value'; --props errors name the flag. (wave 1)
